title: Define transactional acceptance lanes and ambiguity escrow for PRD review
creator: Nina Patel
description: Background: Recent PRD handoffs for Private and Dedicated features exposed repeated ambiguity between scope (what must be built) and implementation assumptions (how teams will build). That ambiguity slows reviews and creates last-minute scope churn. Goal: produce a lightweight, operational definition of 'acceptance lanes' and an 'ambiguity escrow' mechanism so PM/Eng/Design/Legal can close PRD reviews within the review window and surface unresolved items as tracked obligations.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Draft acceptance-lane template (3 lanes: Must, Conditional, Deferred) documented in Confluence and linked in PRD checklists.
A2: Ambiguity escrow added to PRD workflow: unresolved items automatically create a tracked ticket with owner, decision deadline, and rollback/fallback decision.
A3: Engineering and Design review steps include explicit artifacts required per lane (API contract stub, mock flows, perf targets) and reviewers must mark lane-by-lane approval or leave escrow item.
A4: Legal checklist integrated for data residency/KMS requirements; if Legal marks 'requires negotiation' the escrow ticket contains required clauses and target negotiation owner.
A5: Pilot with 2 upcoming PRDs (runtime-telemetry-v2 and dedicated-autoscale-ui) completes within one cycle with retrospective notes and metrics.
A6: Success metric: median PRD review time reduced by 30% for pilot PRDs; number of late-scope changes reduced by 50% compared to previous cycle.
A7: All artifacts and templates live under Confluence space 'PRD Playbook / Acceptance Lanes' and are referenced in the PRD template in Drive.
A8: Security review flagging integrated: any PRD marked 'security_review_required' must have escrow owner and SLA <= 7 business days.
